NUTRITION PLAN FOR BREASTFEEDING
TYPE nutrition
VISIBILITY public
GENERAL GOALS
  GOAL primary nutrition:
    name "Support milk production, recovery, energy, and overall well-being for breastfeeding mother"
RECOMMENDED CALORIES
  NOTE: Energy needs vary; use approximate targets and adjust based on hunger, weight trends, and clinician guidance.
  TARGETS:
    - Estimated daily calories: +300–500 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance or maintenance during lactation if underweight, or as advised by clinician
    - Macronutrient split (approximate):
        protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
        carbohydrates 45–55% of total calories
        fats 25–35% of total calories
STEPS:
  - Prioritize protein at each meal.
  - Distribute calories around workouts and milk production times.
HYDRATION
  GOAL: 3–4 liters water per day (adjust for activity and climate)
  NOTES:
    - Hydration supports milk production and recovery.
    - Include hydrating beverages (water, milk, herbal tea) and high-water-content foods.
MACRONUTRIENT DISTRIBUTION BY MEAL
  - Breakfast:
      - Protein: 25–35 g
      - Carbs: 40–60 g
      - Fats: 10–20 g
  - Lunch:
      - Protein: 25–35 g
      - Carbs: 40–60 g
      - Fats: 10–20 g
  - Dinner:
      - Protein: 25–40 g
      - Carbs: 40–60 g
      - Fats: 10–20 g
  - Snacks (2–3 per day):
      - Protein-rich options: Greek yogurt, cheese, cottage cheese, protein smoothie, edamame, nuts with fruit
      - Carbs: fruit, whole-grain crackers, oats
      - Fats: nuts, seeds, avocado
KEY NUTRIENT TARGETS FOR LACTATION
  - Protein-rich foods at every meal (support tissue repair and milk production)
  - Adequate calcium: 1000 mg/day minimum (dairy or fortified alternatives)
  - Vitamin D: 600–800 IU/day (sunlight + supplementation if needed)
  - Iron: maintain iron intake postpartum (18 mg/day or as advised)
  - Iodine: 150 mcg/day
  - DHA/EPA: ~200–300 mg/day if possible through fish or algae-based supplement
  - Fiber: 25–35 g/day to aid digestion and fullness
FOOD SUGGESTIONS
  - Lean proteins: chicken, turkey, fish (low-mercury), eggs, beans, lentils, tofu
  - Dairy or fortified alternatives: milk, yogurt, cheese, fortified plant milks
  - Whole grains: oats, quinoa, brown rice, whole-wheat bread/pasta
  - Fruits & vegetables: varied colorful produce
  - Healthy fats: olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds
  - Hydration-friendly options: water, milk, 100% fruit juice (in moderation)
FOOD SAFETY AND ALLERGENS
  - Avoid unpasteurized dairy and raw/undercooked eggs or meats
  - If family history of allergies, introduce new allergenic foods gradually
  - Caffeine: limit to 200–300 mg/day; watch infant tolerance
SUPPORTING POSTNATAL RECOVERY
  - Focus on nutrient-dense foods first; consider a simple multivitamin if diet is inadequate (consult clinician)
  - Avoid restrictive dieting; aim for steady energy and mood support
  - Evening meal timing: if sleep is disrupted, include a protein-rich night snack
BREASTFEEDING AWARENESS
  - Milk production responds to regular feeding/pumping; ensure regular meals and snacks
  - If baby has feeding issues or growth concerns, consult pediatrician or lactation consultant
SAMPLE DAY PLAN
  - Breakfast: Greek yogurt with berries, oats, and almonds; coffee or tea
  - Snack: apple with peanut butter
  - Lunch: grilled chicken, quinoa, steamed veggies, olive oil drizzle
  - Snack: hummus with veggie sticks; cheese stick
  - Dinner: salmon or tofu, sweet potato, broccoli; side salad
  - Optional: a protein smoothie post-workout or as a snack
NUTRITION TRACKING REMINDERS
  - Track meals roughly to ensure protein targets; not necessary to count every calorie
  - Monitor weight trends and energy levels; adjust portions gradually
  - Prioritize foods you enjoy to support adherence and breastfeeding comfort
INTEGRATION NOTES
  - This nutrition plan is designed to support breastfeeding, recovery, and gradual return to activity
  - If any contraindications or clinician restrictions arise, adjust caloric intake and macro targets accordingly
  - Coordinate with medical team for any suggestions specific to her post-cesarean recovery and pelvic floor status

CARDIO MODALITIES:
  walking, cycling

SYNTAX RULES:
- Plan remains in WPL-AI format; only canonical exercise names used in the EXERCISE VOCABULARY.
- All rest, sets, reps, and RPE preserved from previous plan.
- This summary consolidates phase structure, progression, progression notes, and nutrition/cardio integration.
